name: Late trip (5-minute rule)
definition: A train run counts as late when its run time over the compared stops is 5 minutes (300 s) or more above the scheduled run time. The MBTA counts a rider trip as reliable when excess trip time is 5 minutes or less.
used_here: late_trip_share, late_trips, trips_compared (run times, not rider trips; no rider weighting)

name: Excess trip time
definition: The MBTA's excess trip time is actual wait plus travel time minus a baseline wait plus travel time, per rider. Here the baseline is the published schedule, not the MBTA's fastest-month baseline, and runs are not rider-weighted.
used_here: train delay (run time minus scheduled run time), average excess per trip
source_name: MBTA OPMI Data Blog: Introducing Excess Trip Time

name: NYC subway comparison
definition: NYC Transit publishes subway reliability as time riders spend beyond the schedule (extra time waiting on the platform and extra time on the train). The same split, wait and ride, is used for rider time lost here.
used_here: rider time lost (excess wait + excess ride)

name: Expected wait
definition: For riders arriving at random times, expected wait = sum(h^2) / (2 * sum(h)) over the gaps h between trains. This is the per-rider form of the OPMI example (each rider waits half the gap they arrive in, so long gaps catch more riders): gaps of 5 and 15 minutes give 6.25 minutes, against 5 for even 10-minute gaps.
used_here: excess wait in rider time lost (actual gaps minus scheduled gaps)
source_name: MBTA OPMI Data Blog: Introducing Excess Trip Time

name: Headway (LAMP)
definition: The gap between a train leaving a stop and the previous train leaving the same stop, from the MBTA's LAMP subway performance files (headway_trunk_seconds; scheduled_headway_trunk for the schedule). Trunk gaps count every train on the shared track, so the Green Line trunk counts all branches.
used_here: long gaps, bunched, gapped, expected wait

name: Bunched and gapped (SFMTA rules)
definition: A departure is bunched when it comes less than 2 minutes after the previous train, and gapped when the gap is more than the scheduled gap plus 5 minutes. These are the SFMTA rules as described by Swiftly.
source_name: Swiftly: How Well Is America Sticking to its Promised Headways?

name: Daily completeness
definition: Trips compared (runs with at least one stop-to-stop comparison) divided by trips in the GTFS schedule published for that date. A line-day is flagged low below 0.8. A low day can be missing data or a real service change (shuttles, diversions).

name: Typical range
definition: The typical value is the median of the same measure on the 28 most recent earlier service dates of the same day type; the typical range is the 25th to 75th percentile (p25 to p75) of those days.
used_here: typical_median, typical_p25, typical_p75 on tiles and line_day_metrics
